Robot Doctor Connection

Robot disconnects or loses the Driver Station mid-match

Connection drops, the DS beeps, the robot stops, then comes back (or not). Below are the 9 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does it happen when the robot gets hit or jolted? Push the robot or tap the frame with your hand while it is running and see if it cuts out.
  • Does it happen right after touching a field wall, field element, or another robot? Think about the last few times. Was the robot touching something metal just before?
  • Does it happen mostly when a big mechanism runs (flywheel, slides, intake) or when you push into something? Try driving around with nothing else running, then run the mechanism by itself.
  • If you wiggle the battery and power cables while it's on, does the hub light flicker or the robot cut out? Gently wiggle the battery plug, the switch wires, and each XT30 at the hub one at a time.
  • Has your Driver Hub / DS phone ever been connected to school or home Wi-Fi? For example, to download an update. Check its saved networks in Android Wi-Fi settings.
  • Does it still drop with no OpMode running (or a simple OpMode that does nothing)? Connect and just sit on the main Driver Station screen, or run an empty OpMode for a couple of minutes.
  • Is the ping on the Driver Station high (over ~50 ms) or jumping around? Ping is shown at the top of the Driver Station app while connected. About 5 ms is great.
  • Does the Driver Station show the voltage dropping to about 9 V or less when it happens? The battery voltage is at the top of the Driver Station screen. Watch it while you drive hard or run the mechanism.
  • Do you have a grounding strap and all USB devices in the USB 3.0 port? The grounding strap is a short wire with a resistor from a spare XT30 port to the frame. The Control Hub's USB 3.0 port is the blue one.
  • Is everything updated this season (Control Hub OS, hub firmware, Robot Controller and Driver Station apps)? The REV Hardware Client shows every version and whether an update is available.
  • Is the Control Hub surrounded by metal or carbon fiber, or mounted next to motors? Look at where the hub sits and what is between it and the drivers.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Loose power connection (XT30 / battery plug)

Compressed XT30 pins or a wiggly battery plug cut power for a split second when the robot gets bumped.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. With the robot on, wiggle the battery cable and each XT30 plug. If the hub light flickers or the DS beeps, you found it.
  2. Look at the male XT30 pins on the hub. Each pin has 4 tines with small gaps; if they are squeezed together, very gently spread them with an X-ACTO blade (REV's fix).
  3. Do not hot glue XT30 plugs. It only hides a bad contact, and the power still drops under impact.
  4. Strap the battery down so it cannot shift, and keep the cable away from sharp screws.
  5. Many teams swap the battery and switch leads to Anderson PowerPole connectors, which wear much better.

Sources: REV · Control Hub troubleshooting · FTC Docs · Annual maintenance · GM0 · Power tips and tricks

2 Static shock (ESD) from the field

Robots build static driving on tiles. When the frame touches metal, the discharge can reset the hub, the IMU, the camera, or Wi-Fi.

How to fix it 30 min

  1. Notice whether it happens right after touching a field element or another robot. That pattern is classic ESD.
  2. Install a FIRST-legal resistive grounding strap (REV-31-1269) from a spare XT30 port to the frame.
  3. Plug cameras and other USB devices into the Control Hub's USB 3.0 port. The USB 2.0 port has a known ESD issue that can knock out Wi-Fi.
  4. Mount electronics on a non-conductive panel (thin plywood, PVC) and keep exposed connector metal more than 3/8" (1 cm) from the frame. Arcs can jump that far.
  5. Snap ferrite chokes onto sensor, encoder, servo, and USB cables, and tape over exposed metal on servo extensions.
  6. Things touching the floor (foam wheels, a dragging intake) build static faster. Many teams wipe the robot with a dryer sheet between matches.

Sources: FTC Docs · Managing ESD · REV · General troubleshooting · GM0 · Wiring guide

3 Too much current draw (brownout)

Flywheels, many servos, or stalled motors pull the battery voltage down until the control system resets or disconnects.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Check whether the problem only happens when a specific mechanism runs. REV lists a disconnect sound, ≤9 V on the DS while running, and motors slower than commanded as brownout signs.
  2. Look for stalled motors: a jammed intake, a slide pushing a hard stop, or an arm held against gravity at full power. Stalls draw huge current.
  3. Stagger big loads in code (spin the flywheel up before you drive hard, not at the same time).
  4. Spread servos across hubs and use a Servo Hub or servo power injector for heavy ones.
  5. Keep the total under the 20 A battery fuse. Flywheels, LEDs, servo injectors, and cameras all add up.
Show battery voltage in telemetry
VoltageSensor battery = hardwareMap.voltageSensor.iterator().next();
// in your loop:
telemetry.addData("Battery (V)", "%.2f", battery.getVoltage());

Sources: REV · Control Hub troubleshooting · FTC Docs · Power management · FTC Docs · Servo power best practices

4 Driver Station remembers other Wi-Fi networks

If the Driver Hub was ever joined to school or home Wi-Fi (for updates), it can hop off the robot's network.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. On the Driver Hub / DS phone, forget every saved Wi-Fi network except the robot.
  2. Toggle Airplane mode on, then make sure Wi-Fi is on and Bluetooth is off.
  3. Re-pair to the robot from the Driver Station app.
  4. Do future updates with the REV Hardware Client instead of joining the DS to the internet.

Sources: FTC Docs · Wireless issues at events · REV · Control Hub troubleshooting

5 Busy or blocked Wi-Fi channel

Crowded channels, school Wi-Fi suppressors, or interference make the link slow and flaky.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Look at the ping on the Driver Station. Around 5 ms is great, under 50 ms is fine, 250 ms+ means a bad link.
  2. If your Driver Station supports it, switch the Control Hub to 5 GHz (REV recommends it), or change to a quieter channel.
  3. At school, ask IT whether a Wi-Fi suppressor is running. It will knock out any robot network.
  4. At an event, tell the FTA or CSA. They can check the channel and move you.

Sources: FTC Docs · Wireless issues at events · REV · Control Hub troubleshooting

6 USB or hub-to-hub cable working loose

Camera, Expansion Hub, and phone cables pull out a little when the robot gets hit.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Push every USB and the hub-to-hub (RS485) cable in firmly and check that nothing hangs loose.
  2. Add strain relief: the REV USB retention mount, 3D printed clips, or zip ties so the cable cannot tug on the port.
  3. Do not wrap cables around the hub, and keep spares. USB ports wear out with repeated plugging.

Sources: REV · Expansion Hub troubleshooting · GM0 · Power tips and tricks · REV · General troubleshooting

7 Your code is blocking the robot controller

A long loop or sleep can make the robot look disconnected: ping climbs and the controls stop responding even though Wi-Fi is fine.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Check whether the problem only happens in one OpMode. An empty OpMode with good ping means the link is fine and the code is the issue.
  2. Never sleep or loop for a long time inside an iterative OpMode's loop(). Use a timer and check it each loop instead.
  3. In LinearOpMode, every while loop must check opModeIsActive().

Sources: FTC Docs · Wireless issues at events · GM0 · Common software issues

8 Out-of-date or mismatched software

Old Control Hub OS, hub firmware, or mismatched Robot Controller / Driver Station apps cause random drops and weird errors.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Update with the REV Hardware Client (Windows) over USB.
  2. FIRST's recommended minimums: Control Hub OS 1.1.6, hub firmware 1.8.2, Robot Controller and Driver Station apps 12.0, Driver Hub OS 1.2.0.
  3. Make sure the Robot Controller and Driver Station app versions match.
  4. If you use Android Studio, update your project to the latest FtcRobotController SDK too.

Sources: FTC Docs · Recommended software versions · REV · Control Hub troubleshooting · FTC Docs · Annual maintenance

9 Control Hub radio is buried in metal

Metal plates and carbon fiber between the hub and the driver block and bounce the Wi-Fi signal.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Move the Control Hub where it has a clear line toward the drivers, away from motors.
  2. Keep sheet metal and carbon fiber out of the path between the hub and the Driver Station.
  3. Do not set the Driver Station on a metal stand. FIRST measured about twice the retries on a metal music stand.

Sources: FTC Docs · Robot Controller mounting · FTC Docs · Wireless issues at events
